Kalshi uses integer cents pricing -- confirmed: prices 1-99 cents
Kalshi supports batch order operations -- confirmed: batch create/cancel supported, up to 20 per call
Kalshi supports order amendment without cancel-and-replace -- confirmed: POST /portfolio/orders/{order_id}/amend
Kalshi supports subaccounts for capital isolation -- confirmed: 0-32 subaccounts
Kalshi demo environment available for paper trading -- confirmed: demo-api.kalshi.co
Kalshi per-market position limits must be queried and enforced -- confirmed: position limits exist per market
Kalshi crypto-price event contracts exist -- confirmed: crypto is a supported market category
USD cash settlement with no blockchain/gas fees -- confirmed: ACH/wire free deposits, no crypto wallets
Kalshi WebSocket available for orderbook streaming -- confirmed: wss://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2
Stateless RSA-PSS authentication with three headers per request -- confirmed: KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY, KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP, KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE
Time-in-force options available for order control -- confirmed: fill_or_kill, good_till_canceled, immediate_or_cancel supported
post_only orders available for maker-only execution -- confirmed: post_only: true supported
invalidated_assumptions: INVALIDATED: 'Settlement fees typically 1-7 cents per contract' -- Kalshi fee structure uses a formula: taker fee = round_up(0.07 * contracts * P * (1-P)), maker fee = round_up(0.0175 * contracts * P * (1-P)). Maximum fee at P=0.50 is 1.75 cents/contract taker. There are NO settlement fees. The spec's fee model based on settlement fees needs complete replacement with the actual taker/maker formula. This significantly changes edge calculations.

INVALIDATED: 'API rate limits must be determined during Phase 1' -- Rate limits are now known: Basic tier is 20 read/s and 10 write/s at signup, Advanced is 30/30, Premier is 100/100 (requires 3.75% monthly volume), Prime is 400/400 (7.5% monthly volume). The spec's target of 50-500 trades/day is well within even Basic tier limits (10 write/s = 864,000 writes/day).

INVALIDATED: 'Batch operations up to 20 orders per call' -- Batch create/cancel is supported but BatchCancelOrders counts as 0.2 per transaction against rate limits. The spec's assumption of 20 per batch needs verification against actual batch size limits.

PARTIALLY INVALIDATED: '85-98% documented win rate for latency arb' -- This figure is from Polymarket, not Kalshi. Debate accepted change: replace with 'to be determined in Phase 1'. Kalshi's regulated market structure with institutional market makers likely produces significantly lower rates.

Make profitability success criteria conditional on which strategy tiers pass Phase 1 validation
Add Kalshi WebSocket update frequency measurement as Phase 1 deliverable

specs_validated.title: Non-Directional Liquidity Capture & Market Making System
confirmed_assumptions: Kalshi operates a CLOB (Central Limit Order Book) -- confirmed
Kalshi supports limit orders with post_only flag for maker-only execution -- confirmed: post_only: true ensures maker-only orders
Kalshi supports order amendment preserving queue priority -- confirmed: POST /portfolio/orders/{order_id}/amend
Kalshi supports batch order creation and cancellation -- confirmed: batch operations supported
RSA-PSS per-request signing authentication -- confirmed: stateless, no login endpoint
Kalshi per-market position limits exist and must be enforced -- confirmed
Kalshi demo environment available for paper trading validation -- confirmed
Kalshi subaccounts available for capital isolation -- confirmed: up to 32
Binance/Coinbase WebSocket feeds available for reference price tracking -- confirmed: public streams available
Order groups available for aggregate risk management -- confirmed: POST /portfolio/order_groups/create
invalidated_assumptions: INVALIDATED: 'Settlement fees typically 1-7 cents per contract' -- Kalshi uses taker/maker fee formulas, NOT settlement fees. Taker: round_up(0.07 * contracts * P * (1-P)), Maker: round_up(0.0175 * contracts * P * (1-P)). NO settlement fees. This fundamentally changes the market-making economics: (1) maker fees at ~0.44 cents max at P=0.50 are very favorable for market making, (2) the spec's settlement-fee-aware spread floor needs recalculation using maker fee formula, (3) SettlementRecyclingEngine fee calculations need complete revision, (4) SpreadCaptureTracker net spread calculations change significantly.

INVALIDATED: 'FIFO vs pro-rata matching engine -- to be confirmed in Phase 0' -- CLOB structure with post_only support strongly implies price-time (FIFO) priority, consistent with standard CLOB implementations. The spec can proceed with FIFO as working assumption while Phase 0 confirms.

INVALIDATED: 'Maker vs taker fee structure -- whether maker rebates exist' -- Now known: maker fee is 0.0175 * P * (1-P) per contract, taker fee is 0.07 * P * (1-P). No rebates, but maker fees are 4x lower than taker fees. This heavily favors the market-making strategy since all ladder orders are maker orders (post_only: true).

INVALIDATED: 'Batch operations up to 20 orders per call' -- Batch operations are supported but specific per-batch size limits and rate limit counting (BatchCancelOrders = 0.2 per transaction) need verification.

PARTIALLY INVALIDATED: 'API rate limits -- to be determined' -- Rate limits now known at 4 tiers. Basic tier (20 read/s, 10 write/s) may be insufficient for HF market making with 10-15 level ladders refreshed every 3 seconds. The spec should target Advanced tier (30/30) at minimum, or Premier (100/100) for full operation.
remaining_unknowns: Position merging/netting: Can YES+NO positions be combined for early capital release, or must positions be held to expiry? This is the most critical remaining unknown for capital efficiency.
FIFO matching confirmation: While CLOB structure implies FIFO, explicit confirmation from Kalshi documentation is needed.
WebSocket update frequency and granularity for HF order management
Exact batch operation size limits and rate limit impact
Whether order amendment truly preserves FIFO queue position (documented but needs empirical verification)
Crypto contract liquidity depth sufficient for simultaneous YES and NO ladder deployment
Whether rate limits at Basic tier (10 write/s) are sufficient for ladder management, or if Advanced/Premier tier is required

invalidated_assumptions: INVALIDATED: 'Settlement fees 1-7 cents per contract' referenced in fee-aware minimum edge thresholds -- Kalshi uses taker/maker fee formulas, NOT settlement fees. knowledge_gaps_requiring_research: CRITICAL: All 5 specs assume settlement fees of 1-7 cents per contract. The actual Kalshi fee structure uses taker/maker formulas with NO settlement fees.
